description: Balaji Srinivasan is a technology entrepreneur, investor and author, known as a former Coinbase CTO and a16z general partner, and as founder of Network School and author of The Network State.
Bill Ackman founded and runs Pershing Square, and chairs Pershing Square Inc. and Howard Hughes Holdings.
Bill Gates is chair of the Gates Foundation and author of the Gates Notes blog.
Daniela Amodei is a co-founder and President of Anthropic.
Dario Amodei is the co-founder and CEO of Anthropic and a former VP of Research at OpenAI.
Demis Hassabis is an AI researcher and entrepreneur who co-founded DeepMind, has led Isomorphic Labs, and has held senior leadership roles at Google DeepMind.
Eliezer Yudkowsky is a writer, co-founder and research fellow of MIRI, founder of LessWrong, and co-author of "If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies".
Elon Musk is a technology entrepreneur and executive who is CEO of Tesla and SpaceX and leads Neuralink and The Boring Company.

Gary Marcus has written six books, including Rebooting AI and Taming Silicon Valley. Bloomberg describes him as an NYU Emeritus Professor, and he comments on AI and writes the "Marcus on AI" Substack.
Jeff Bezos is an entrepreneur who founded Amazon, where he is executive chairman, and who also founded Blue Origin and is co-CEO of Project Prometheus.
Jensen Huang is the co-founder, president and chief executive officer of NVIDIA, and a member of its board of directors.
Jeremy Grantham is an investor who co-founded the asset managers GMO and Batterymarch, is listed by GMO as its long-term investment strategist, and co-authored 'The Making of a Permabear'.
Jim Cramer is a television commentator and author who hosts CNBC's "Mad Money", co-anchors "Squawk on the Street" and founded TheStreet.
Marc Andreessen co-founded and is a General Partner of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and earlier co-created Mosaic and co-founded Netscape.
Mark Zuckerberg is a technology entrepreneur who co-founded Facebook and serves as founder, chairman and chief executive officer of Meta Platforms.
Michael Burry is an investor who founded Scion Capital and Scion Asset Management, was portrayed in The Big Short, and is widely covered for his portfolio and warnings about an AI bubble.

Nassim Nicholas Taleb is described as a university professor and mathematical statistician, and he is the author of the Incerto series, which includes Fooled by Randomness (Penguin Random House, 2001) and The Black Swan.

Nate Silver is a statistician and political analyst who founded FiveThirtyEight and now publishes the Silver Bulletin newsletter, where he runs a Trump approval tracker, pollster ratings and a 2026 midterm forecast.
Nouriel Roubini is an economist, professor emeritus at NYU Stern, CEO of Roubini Macro Associates and a columnist known for forecasting the 2008 financial crisis.
Peter Thiel is an entrepreneur and venture capitalist who co-founded PayPal and Palantir Technologies and founded Founders Fund.
Ray Dalio is an investor and author who founded the hedge fund Bridgewater Associates and wrote the 2017 book Principles: Life and Work, among other books.

Ray Kurzweil is an author of books on artificial intelligence and the technological singularity, including The Singularity Is Near, The Singularity Is Nearer, The Age of Spiritual Machines and How to Create a Mind; he received the 1999 National Medal of Technology and Innovation, became Director of Engineering at Google and co-founded Singularity University.
Rodney Brooks is a roboticist who was director of the MIT AI Lab/CSAIL from 1997 to 2007, co-founded iRobot and Robust.AI, and founded Rethink Robotics.
Sam Altman is a technology executive who co-founded OpenAI and serves as its CEO.
Satya Nadella is the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Microsoft, which he has led as CEO since 2014.
Scott Alexander is a writer known for his blogs Astral Codex Ten and Slate Star Codex and for fiction including Unsong.
Steven Pinker is the Johnstone Family Professor of Psychology at Harvard University and the author of thirteen popular books, including The Language Instinct and Enlightenment Now.

Tyler Cowen is an economist and commentator who holds the Holbert L. Harris Chair of Economics at George Mason University and co-founded the Marginal Revolution blog, which he has written daily since 2003.
Vinod Khosla founded Khosla Ventures and co-founded Sun Microsystems, and Forbes ranks him No. 1 on its 2026 Midas List.
Warren Buffett led Berkshire Hathaway as chairman from 1970 and as CEO until January 1, 2026, and now serves as chairman emeritus and a board member.

Yann LeCun is a computer scientist and AI researcher who shared the 2018 ACM Turing Award, is a Jacob T. Schwartz Professor at NYU, and is Executive Chairman of AMI Labs after serving as Meta's Chief AI Scientist from 2018 to 2025.
